title: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, retiring the Flash brand
subtitle: The new everyday model is 2.5x faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash and ties the heavier Argon on Google's intelligence index.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12, rolling it out through Google Search, the Gemini app, the Gemini API and AI Studio. The model replaces Gemini 3.8 Flash as the company's default everyday option. Google says Hydrogen completes tasks about 2.5 times faster than its predecessor and scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index — one point ahead of the heavier Gemini 4 Argon. API pricing starts at $1.50 per million input tokens, and the model ships with a 1,048,576-token context window.

Hydrogen is the first model in the Gemini 4 line to drop 'Flash' from its name. The branding change signals that Google no longer treats fast, cheap inference as a lower tier. The lineup is now cut around element names — Argon, Carbon, Hydrogen — with each model positioned by workload rather than by size. Inside Google Antigravity, a new Orchestrator feature can hand planning to Carbon and execution to Hydrogen within a single task. That split is the shape Google expects most agent runs to take.

The release lands in the same week as OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet and its Daybreak security agents, and five days after Anthropic's Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2. Every frontier lab is now shipping agent-oriented models and the infrastructure to wire them to the world. The Gemini app crossed one billion monthly active users in August, and Google has used that reach to push free users onto automatic model selection — so Hydrogen will land in many hands without anyone asking for it by name.

A takeaway for learners: model families now trade off along three axes, not two. Speed, cost and raw capability used to line up — bigger was slower and more expensive, smaller was faster and cheaper. A model that beats a larger sibling on an intelligence benchmark while running faster breaks that intuition. Pay attention to the benchmark you care about for your task, not the tier label the vendor prints on the box.
